title: Mini-surge sprint scratchpad: coverage heuristics & quick picks
content:
Purpose:
Quick pragmatic tracker for an expected short-term surge window (48–96h). Not a project plan — just who-to-call, fast fallbacks, and cheap heuristics we can apply to keep token/unit cost and latencies within guardrails while capacity is stretched.

Table (rows = routes / shards / presence):
Route | Primary owner | Backup owner(s) | Expected QPS delta | Acceptable latency bump (p95, ms) | Quick heuristic (route-level) | Temp routing action | Estimated ops time (mins) | Notes
ingest-realtime | Marco H. | Leah K., Daniel P. | +18% | +30ms | if KV-cache-hit-rate > 65% keep; else divert to dedicated-small | route->dedicated-small (canary 10%) | 25 | watch tokenization spike at hour 2
chat-convo-stream | Leah K. | Marco H. | +40% | +50ms | enable batching (max 40ms), q4 quant for non-prod | enable batching + q4 fallback for non-prod | 40 | ensure canary only for non-SLA customers
embeddings-bulk | Daniel P. | Infra-oncall | +120% | +100ms | auto-shard by customer domain; short-circuit duplicate payloads | set domain-shard threshold 50qps -> split | 30 | dedupe gives big wins for search re-indexing burst
autocomplete-low | Leah K. | Marco H. | +12% | +20ms | aggressively cache prefix results for 10s | increase cache TTL for short prefixes | 15 | regression risk: newer prompt templates may need invalidation
rerank-critical | Marco H. | SRE | +6% | +15ms | keep strict SLO; if capacity short, fallback to cheaper model variant v0.9 | fallback path -> rerank-lite | 10 | track quality delta with sample set

Quick heuristics (rationale + how-to):
- Heuristic A: Cache-first for bursty short requests. If > 50% of requests are <= 8 tokens, prefer prefix cache TTL 8–15s. Action: bump edge TTL, track cache hit ratio hourly.
- Heuristic B: Quantization-only for non-SLA or test traffic. If route labeled non-prod or traceable to sandbox orgs, switch to q4/q8 to free GPU memory.
- Heuristic C: Split by customer domain for large batch jobs. For any customer causing >30% of route QPS, shard to separate worker pool to reduce head-of-line blocking.

Short-run rollout cadence (hours):
T0 (detect spike): notify channel #ops-mini-surge, set read-only of routing rules to team leads, enable telemetry sampling 10% -> 100%
T+15m: apply per-route heuristics (cache TTLs, batching thresholds) with 1% canary
T+45m: escalate to 10% canary + open backups (dedicated pool) if p95 > target
T+2h: full policy apply if metrics stable (latency within acceptable bump)

Ownership playbook (one-liners):
- Primary owner: triage, set canary, own Slack updates.
- Backup owner: prepare rollback plan & infra ticket.
- Infra-oncall: stand ready to spin dedicated-small pools, confirm capacity.
- SRE: metric sanity checks and ensure alerts escalations are annotated.

Open questions / TODOs (fast list):
- Confirm dedicated-small spin-up time for region-eu-west (Marco).
- Agree on acceptable p95 bump for embeddings-bulk (Product ops + SRE).
- Create tiny eval set (50 queries) to compare q4 quant vs full for rerank-critical (Leah).
- Add a lightweight telemetry tag for "mini-surge" in request trace (Infra).

Post-surge notes (short template to fill):
- Surge start / end time: 
- Primary root causes: 
- Top 3 mitigations that mattered: 
- Metric deltas (QPS, p95, errors): 
- Follow-ups (owners & rough ETA):

Slack links: 
- initial alert thread: https://slack.redwood.com/archives/C01ABCDEF/p20340310-081500
- post-mortem draft (starter): CONFLUENCE-4567

Purpose reminder: keep this small, shareable. If something needs a longer runbook, move to product-ops/runbooks/mini-surge-full-notes (confluence).

Notes to self: this sheet is intentionally noisy and partial — use for fast decisioning, not as permanent source of truth.
summary: Short ad-hoc spreadsheet for 48–96h surge: per-route owners, quick fallbacks, batching/caching heuristics, and an hour-by-hour rollout checklist. Meant to be edited in the moment and trimmed into a post-surge follow-up.
